newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Arrangers confirm CITIC in HK$8 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Arrangers confirm CITIC in HK$8 bln loan.

text.p: CITIC Pacific has mandated five banks to arrange a HK$8.0 billion loan facility, the arrangers confirmed on Tuesday.

Red Chip CITIC Pacific has mandated Banque Nationale de Paris Hong Kong branch (facility agent), Chase Manhattan Asia (bookrunner), HSBC Investment Bank Asia (bookrunner), Hang Seng Bank (documentation) and J.P. Morgan Securities Asia (signing and publicity) as coordinating arrangers for the loan.
The facility is fully underwritten by the five coordinating arrangers.
The facility is structured in two tranches.

Tranche A of HK$5.0 billion is structured as a 24-month revolving credit converting to a term loan. Tranche A has a final maturity of five years and pays an interest margin of 45 basis points per annum.
Tranche B of HK$3 billion is structured as a seven-year term loan facility. It pays an interest margin of 50 basis points per annum.
The coordinating arrangers said that syndication will begin after an arranger group is formed. They said formation of the arranger group would begin shortly.
Earlier today, bankers said CITIC Pacific was planning to raise HK$8.0 billion to help fund its investment in China Light and Power Co.

They said the loan would be used for working capital and to repay a short-term HK$12.5 billion bridging loan signed in February to help fund the company's HK$16.25 billion acquisition of 20 percent of CLP.
The HK$12.5 billion bridging loan had a tenor of less than one year and was not syndicated.
On May 9, CITIC Pacific said it had agreed to sell a 7.74 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd for HK$11.4 billion.
The coordinating arrangers said proceeds of the HK$8.0 billion loan would be used for refinancing of existing debts and for general corporate purposes.
